facts.fact: 1942年12月5日Béatrice和Fanny在Neuilly被捕（没戴金星）；名字记入16区警察局Consignes Provisoires台账；台账里她们名字旁只有一个词："Juive"（犹太女人）。
facts.anchor: On the afternoon of December 5, Béatrice and Fanny were stopped. There was no struggle, just uniforms, and the demand for identity papers. They gave them, but it didn’t matter.

facts.fact: 台账里只有一个词"Juive"；Irène Anspach（表亲）在场却未被捕——"太随机而非仁慈"；Béatrice递给她金手链（gourmette）；archivist Le Tarnec至今不解"为何她没被捕"。
facts.anchor: In the ledger, there was just one word in the columns by their names: Juive.

facts.fact: Rudi de Mérode（原名Frédéric Martin）自称"王子"，领导Gestapo de Neuilly（法国准军事团伙）；在Béatrice家附近70号别墅运作；劫掠、酷刑、30%佣金；涉及>500人驱逐。
facts.anchor: He was a thief with aristocratic pretensions, a man who called himself “the prince” and led the Gestapo de Neuilly, a French paramilitary gang that worked hand in hand with the Germans, doing the things the Germans preferred not to be seen doing.

facts.fact: 战后内政部统计Mérode财产：近10亿法郎（今约$9400万）；现金、珠宝、黄金塞在柜子里、埋在花园里；他逃往西班牙马德里，自称"Prince de Mérode"，约1970年后死于西班牙，从未被追诉。
facts.anchor: After the war, the Interior Ministry tallied up Mérode’s fortune: nearly 1 billion francs, about $94 million today. Cash, jewels, gold—bundled in cupboards, buried in gardens.

facts.fact: Béatrice公寓被清空：三架Pleyel钢琴、Louis XVI钟、Théodore肖像；14,933股房产股份被冻结；"一切消失得如此之快：Léon的音乐、Kérylos档案、图纸、信件。还有书，四千本，皮面装订。"
facts.anchor: It had all vanished so quickly: Léon’s music, the archive of the Kérylos villa, the drawings and architectural plans, the letters. And the books, four thousand of them, leather-bound.
